name: Goal-Line Haley Edge Rush
formation: Goal Line Heavy, Twin TE Right vs Over-Shifted Speed Front
frontName: Over Shift 4-3 with Hand-Down Wide End

summary.motive: Commit the goal-line protection strong with an over shift and slant package, then let one isolated edge rusher decide a short-field possession.
summary.keyDefender: The hand-down wide end rushing off the right edge
summary.whyItWorks: Goal-line slide protection must honor four interior threats and the back must take the Mike dog, so the wide end is guaranteed a one-on-one he usually wins.
summary.failureMode: The tight end stays on the edge and doubles the wide end with the tackle, freeing the nose for a clean three-step throw to the flat.

beats.title: The Over Shift Loads the Strong Side
beats.text: Four defenders crowd the twin-tight-end strength before the snap, so the offense tilts its slide protection strong — exactly where Jimmy Johnson wants the arithmetic committed.

beats.title: The Interior Slants Pin Four Blockers
beats.text: The tackles stagger their slants into strong A and strong B while the weak end crashes off the snap, gluing Center, both guards, and the snapping tight end to blocks they cannot leave.

beats.title: Haley Wins the Solo Edge
beats.text: The tight end snapped down instead of helping outside, leaving the right tackle alone against Charles Haley’s hand-down burst; one stab and a speed-bull later the edge is gone.

beats.title: Corner Crush at the Stripe
beats.text: The climbing quarterback steps away from the interior surge directly into Haley’s flatten, and the ball comes out at the goal line — penetration philosophy cashed into points.

relations.tell: The strong tight end snaps down to the slanting tackle at the snap — a true goal-line run keeps him glued to the wide end instead.
